notes.front: What is Azure Content Understanding?
notes.back: A Foundry Tool that uses generative AI to turn documents, images, video and audio into output in a format you define.
notes.explanation: It is available as part of the Microsoft Foundry resource and is Microsoft’s information extraction service.
notes.example: Like a mailroom that opens every parcel, whatever its shape, and fills in the same form for each.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools is a Foundry Tool that's available as part of the Microsoft Foundry Resource in the Azure portal. It uses generative AI to process and ingest many types of content, including documents, images, videos, and audio, into a user-defined output format.

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is an analyzer?
notes.back: The core component that defines how content is processed: its content extraction settings, field schema and model deployments.
notes.explanation: Once configured, it applies the same settings to all incoming data.
notes.example: Like a recipe card: once written, every batch is made the same way.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: The core component that defines how your content is processed. It configures content extraction settings, field extraction schema, and model deployments. Once configured, the analyzer consistently applies these settings to all incoming data.

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is content extraction?
notes.back: Turning unstructured input into normalised, structured text and metadata, such as text, tables and layout from documents.
notes.explanation: For audio and video it transcribes speech and identifies key visual elements.
notes.example: Like typing up a scanned file faithfully, headings and tables included, before anyone analyses it.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Transforms unstructured input into normalized, structured text and metadata. Extracts text using optical character recognition (OCR), identifies selection marks and barcodes, detects formulas, and recognizes layout elements like paragraphs, sections, and tables. For audio and video, transcribes speech and identifies key visual elements.

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is a field schema?
notes.back: Your definition of the fields to produce, each with a name, type and description.
notes.explanation: At run time the generative model fills those fields from the content.
notes.example: Like the column headings of a spreadsheet you want filled in.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools video solutions”, “Custom fields” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Use a `fieldSchema` object where each entry defines a field's name, type, and description. At run-time, the generative model fills those fields for every segment.

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is field extraction?
notes.back: Generating structured key-value pairs from the content, based on the field schema you define.
notes.explanation: Fields can be produced by three methods: extract, classify and generate.
notes.example: Like a clerk filling in the “date”, “supplier” and “total” boxes from each invoice.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Generates structured key-value pairs based on your defined schema. See service limits for supported field types. Fields can be generated via three methods:

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is segmentation?
notes.back: Dividing documents or videos into logical sections for targeted processing.
notes.explanation: For example, splitting a document by document type, or a video into scenes.
notes.example: Like splitting a bundle of post into letters, bills and leaflets before handling each pile.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Divides documents or videos into logical sections for targeted processing. Configured using the `enableSegment` property in the analyzer schema. Enables breaking content into meaningful chunks, such as splitting a document by document type or dividing a video into scenes.

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is source grounding?
notes.back: Identifying the specific regions of the content where each field value was extracted or generated.
notes.explanation: It lets people quickly check a value by tracing it back to its origin.
notes.example: Like a footnote that points to the exact line of the contract a figure came from.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Identifies the specific regions in the content where each value was extracted or generated. Source grounding allows users in automation scenarios to quickly verify the correctness of field values by tracing them back to their origin in the source content.

notes.front: What is a prebuilt analyzer?
notes.back: A ready-to-use analyzer with domain-specific extraction for common tasks, such as invoices, identity documents or call recordings.
notes.explanation: Prebuilt analyzers are powered by knowledge bases of real-world document examples.
notes.example: Like a printed tax form: the boxes are already designed; you just use it.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Azure Content Understanding prebuilt analyzers provide a set of domain-specific extraction capabilities that go beyond predefined schemas. They're powered by knowledge bases of real-world document examples.

notes.front: What is a custom analyzer?
notes.back: An analyzer you define for your own needs, often starting from a prebuilt analyzer used as a template.
notes.explanation: A prebuilt analyzer can serve as the starting point.
notes.example: Like altering an off-the-peg suit to fit, instead of weaving the cloth.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Customize prebuilt analyzers” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Use any prebuilt analyzer as a template for creating a custom analyzer that better fits your specific needs.

notes.front: What is Content Understanding Studio?
notes.back: A web portal that complements Foundry for Content Understanding, optimised for improving analyzer performance.
notes.explanation: It suits teams moving from Document Intelligence and supports improving custom analyzers with data labelling.
notes.example: Like a specialist workshop next to the main factory floor.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Content Understanding web portals” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Content Understanding Studio**: A complementary UX experience, Content Understanding Studio enables a smooth transition if you're moving from Document Intelligence. It offers an experience optimized for analyzer performance improvement including improving custom analyzers using data labeling techniques.

notes.front: In Content Understanding, what is a guardrail?
notes.back: The safety control on a Foundry model deployment that decides whether potentially harmful content is blocked or allowed through with warnings.
notes.explanation: Blocking can limit field extraction or stop the analysis completing.
notes.example: Like a newsroom editor who can spike a story or let it run with a warning note.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Guardrails in Microsoft Foundry” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: The guardrail assigned to your Foundry model deployment controls whether potentially harmful content is blocked or allowed through with warnings. Blocking can limit field extraction or prevent analysis from completing.

notes.front: What must you create before you can use Content Understanding?
notes.back: A Foundry resource in Azure.
notes.explanation: Content Understanding is a Foundry service.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Content Understanding web portals” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Content Understanding is a Foundry service. To use Content Understanding, you must create a Foundry Azure Resource.

notes.front: Do you need complex prompt engineering to extract fields with Content Understanding?
notes.back: No. You define a schema to extract, classify or generate field values.
notes.explanation: Field extraction is designed to make structured output from unstructured content simpler.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Why use Content Understanding?” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Content Understanding's field extraction makes it easier to generate structured output from unstructured content. Define a schema to extract, classify, or generate field values with no complex prompt engineering.

notes.front: Which field method takes values directly as they appear in the content, such as a date on a receipt?
notes.back: Extract.
notes.explanation: It is supported for documents only.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Extract**: Directly extract values as they appear in the input content (supported for documents only), such as dates from receipts or item details from invoices.

notes.front: Which field method picks a value from a predefined set of categories, such as call sentiment?
notes.back: Classify.
notes.explanation: It can also route content to the correct analyzer.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Classify**: Classify content from a predefined set of categories, such as call sentiment or chart type, and route it to the correct analyzer for analysis.

notes.front: Which field method freely produces values, such as a summary of an audio conversation?
notes.back: Generate.
notes.explanation: It creates new values from the input rather than copying or categorising.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Generate**: Generate values freely from input data, such as summarizing an audio conversation or creating scene descriptions from videos.

notes.front: Can you use the Extract field method on a video?
notes.back: No. Extract is supported for documents only.
notes.explanation: For audio and video, use Classify or Generate.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Directly extract values as they appear in the input content (supported for documents only)

notes.front: What range do Content Understanding confidence scores take, and what do high scores allow?
notes.back: 0 to 1; high scores allow straight-through processing in automation.
notes.explanation: They estimate the reliability of each extracted field value.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Provides reliability estimates from 0 to 1 for each extracted field value. High scores indicate accurate data extraction, enabling straight-through processing in automation workflows.

notes.front: Which document analyzer setting turns on confidence scores and grounding?
notes.back: `estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence`.
notes.explanation: The same setting enables both features.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Enabled using the `estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence` setting in document analyzers.

notes.front: What should you do with low-confidence or poorly grounded extractions?
notes.back: Route them for human review, and let high-confidence, grounded results continue automatically.
notes.explanation: This keeps accuracy high while limiting manual work.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools document solutions”, “Field extraction” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Use confidence scores and source grounding to route low-confidence or insufficiently grounded extractions for human review. Continue high-confidence, grounded results through downstream automated workflows.

notes.front: Whose generative model deployments does Content Understanding use?
notes.back: Your own deployments of supported Foundry generative and embedding models.
notes.explanation: It uses them for field extraction, figure analysis and other AI-powered features.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: You bring your own deployments of supported generative models and text-embedding models for training examples. Content Understanding uses these models for field extraction, figure analysis, and other AI-powered features.

notes.front: In what two formats can Content Understanding supply its final output?
notes.back: Markdown, for search and retrieval, or `JSON` matching your schema, for automation and analytics.
notes.explanation: You choose the format that suits the downstream workflow.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Content can be output as Markdown for search and retrieval scenarios, or as structured JSON matching your defined schema for automation and analytics workflows.

notes.front: What are two categories of analyzer that Content Understanding provides?
notes.back: Two of: content extraction, base, RAG, domain-specific and utility analyzers.
notes.explanation: Each category supports a different kind of scenario.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Analyzer types” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Content Understanding provides several categories of analyzers to support different scenarios:

notes.front: What does prebuilt-read provide?
notes.back: Basic OCR: words, paragraphs, formulas and barcodes, without layout analysis.
notes.explanation: It gives foundational text extraction.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “prebuilt-read” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Extracts content elements such as words, paragraphs, formulas, and barcodes from documents. * Provides basic optical character recognition (OCR) capabilities. * Provides foundational text extraction without layout analysis.

notes.front: What does prebuilt-layout add beyond basic text extraction?
notes.back: Layout elements such as tables and figures, and document structure such as sections and formatting.
notes.explanation: It provides detailed layout information beyond basic text.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “prebuilt-layout” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Extracts content and layout elements such as words, figures, paragraphs, and tables from documents. * Identifies document structure, including sections and formatting.

notes.front: From which analyzers can you currently derive a custom analyzer?
notes.back: Only the four base analyzers: prebuilt-audio, prebuilt-document, prebuilt-image and prebuilt-video.
notes.explanation: Deriving means naming a parent with the baseAnalyzerId property. Copying any prebuilt analyzer’s definition as a template is a separate route.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Base analyzers” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: When you create a custom analyzer, include one of these base analyzers by using the `baseAnalyzerId` property. * `prebuilt-audio` - Base audio processing * `prebuilt-document` - Base document processing * `prebuilt-image` - Base image processing * `prebuilt-video` - Base video processing > [!NOTE] > Currently, you can only derive custom analyzers from this set of four base analyzers.

notes.front: How do you create a custom analyzer from a prebuilt template by sending web requests?
notes.back: `GET` the prebuilt analyzer’s definition, edit it, then `PUT` it under a new analyzer name.
notes.explanation: The definition returned includes the field schema and configuration options.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Get an analyzer definition” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: The response returns a JSON definition with the field schema and configuration options. You can edit this definition and create your own analyzer based on it.

notes.front: Which request analyses content with a prebuilt analyzer?
notes.back: A `POST` to the analyze endpoint, such as `/analyzers/prebuilt-idDocument:analyze`.
notes.explanation: Replace the analyzer name with the one that matches your scenario.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Use prebuilt analyzers” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: To analyze content by using a prebuilt analyzer, make a POST request to the analyze endpoint: ```http POST /analyzers/prebuilt-idDocument:analyze ``` Replace `prebuilt-idDocument` with the analyzer ID that matches your scenario.

notes.front: What are two kinds of document prebuilt-idDocument handles?
notes.back: Two of: driving licences, identity cards, residency permits, passports, among others.
notes.explanation: It is a domain-specific analyzer for identity documents.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Identity documents” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: `prebuilt-idDocument` - Driver licenses, identification cards (IDs), residency permits, passports (worldwide)

notes.front: Which prebuilt analyzer is recommended for document ingestion in RAG workflows?
notes.back: prebuilt-documentSearch.
notes.explanation: It produces chunked output ready for embedding and vector indexing.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “prebuilt-documentSearch” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Produces chunked output ready for embedding and vector indexing, preserving document structure across chunk boundaries with support for both fixed-size and layout-aware semantic chunking. * Supports a [wide range of file formats](/azure/ai-services/content-understanding/service-limits#input-file-limits) including PDF, images, Office documents, and text files. * Recommended for document ingestion in RAG workflows.

notes.front: What does prebuilt-imageSearch produce for an image?
notes.back: A one-paragraph description of the image content, plus visual content for search and retrieval.
notes.explanation: It analyses images to generate descriptions and insights.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “prebuilt-imageSearch” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Analyzes images to generate descriptions and insights. * Generates a one-paragraph description of the image content. * Extracts visual content for search and retrieval applications.

notes.front: If your main goal is to extract text from images, should you use an image analyzer?
notes.back: No. Consider a document field extraction schema instead.
notes.explanation: Image analyzers are not optimised for analysis based mainly on extracted text.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools image solutions”, “Get started” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Image analyzers are not optimized for scenarios where analysis is based primarily on extracted text. If your main goal is to extract and analyze text from images, consider using a document field extraction schema instead.

notes.front: What are two use cases the documentation gives for extracting information from images?
notes.back: Two of: RAG applications, financial chart analysis, manufacturing quality control, shelf analysis and inventory.
notes.explanation: Each needs structured data drawn from image content.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools image solutions”, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools image solutions” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Manufacturing quality control:** Automate the detection of defects and anomalies, such as scratches, cracks, or misalignments, in production lines and manufacturing environments.

notes.front: What are two things document content extraction captures besides printed text?
notes.back: Two of: handwriting, selection marks, barcodes, formulas, figures, tables, sections, among others.
notes.explanation: It preserves the document’s structure through layout analysis.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools document solutions”, “Content extraction” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Content extraction precisely captures printed and handwritten text while it preserves the document's structure through advanced layout analysis: - Content analysis - **Text**: Processes multilingual content, including both machine-printed and handwritten text from hundreds of languages. - **Selection marks**: Identifies and extracts selection indicators such as checkboxes

notes.front: Besides transcription, what do Content Understanding audio analyzers do for conversations?
notes.back: Diarisation, and extraction of structured fields such as summaries, sentiment and key topics.
notes.explanation: You can start by customising an audio analyzer template in the Foundry portal.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools audio solutions”, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools audio solutions” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Audio analyzers enable transcription and diarization for conversational audio and extract structured fields such as summaries, sentiment, and key topics. Customize an audio analyzer template for your needs in the Foundry portal to start generating results.

notes.front: In what format do all Content Understanding audio analyzers produce transcripts?
notes.back: `WebVTT`, separated by speaker.
notes.explanation: Prebuilt audio analyzers use multilingual transcription by default.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools audio solutions”, “Prebuilt audio analyzers” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: All audio analyzers generate transcripts in standard WEBVTT format separated by speaker. > [!NOTE] > > Prebuilt analyzers are set to use multilingual transcription and `returnDetails` enabled.

notes.front: What are two outputs of the prebuilt-callCenter analyzer?
notes.back: Two of: a transcript with speaker roles, call summary, call sentiment, mentioned companies and people, call categories.
notes.explanation: It is the prebuilt analyzer for post-call analysis.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools audio solutions”, “Prebuilt audio analyzers” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Post-call analysis (prebuilt-callCenter)**. Analyze call recordings to generate: * Conversation transcripts with speaker role detection results. * A call summary. * Call sentiment.

notes.front: In what two stages does Content Understanding process a video?
notes.back: Content extraction (transcripts and shots), then field extraction and segmentation by a generative model.
notes.explanation: Field extraction builds on what content extraction captured.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools video solutions”, “Capabilities” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: The service operates in two stages. The first stage, content extraction, involves capturing foundational metadata such as transcripts and shots. The second stage, field extraction, uses a generative model to produce custom fields and perform segmentation.

notes.front: About how many frames per second does the video analyzer inspect, and what is the risk?
notes.back: About one; rapid motions or single-frame events might be missed.
notes.explanation: Frames are sampled, not every frame is analysed.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools video solutions”, “Technical constraints and limitations” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: The analyzer inspects about one frame per second. Rapid motions or single-frame events might be missed.

notes.front: To what size are sampled video frames resized, and what can be lost?
notes.back: 512 x 512 pixels; small text or distant objects can be lost.
notes.explanation: The resizing limits how much fine detail the model sees.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools video solutions”, “Technical constraints and limitations” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Sampled frames are resized to 512 pixels square. Small text or distant objects can be lost.

notes.front: How does prebuilt-videoSearch decide where to split a video?
notes.back: By topic shifts, scene changes or visual cues.
notes.explanation: It then gives each segment a transcript and a description.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “prebuilt-videoSearch” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Analyzes videos to extract transcripts and descriptions for each segment. * Automatically segments videos into meaningful sections based on topic shifts, scene changes, or visual cues.

notes.front: Which Content Understanding API version should production workloads use?
notes.back: `2025-11-01` (generally available).
notes.explanation: The `2026-06-01-preview` version is for evaluating new capabilities.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Content Understanding Features by version” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Use API version `2025-11-01` (GA) for production workloads, and use API version `2026-06-01-preview` to evaluate new capabilities announced in the Build 2026 wave.

notes.front: Can a Content Understanding analysis succeed even when a guardrail stops some field values?
notes.back: Yes. It can succeed with warnings, returning extracted content without those fields.
notes.explanation: Guardrails can restrict field generation while keeping the extracted source content.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Guardrails in Microsoft Foundry” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Guardrails can restrict field generation while preserving extracted source content. Analysis can therefore succeed with warnings even when some field values aren't returned.

notes.front: An analyzer must copy the policy number exactly as printed on scanned insurance forms. Which field method fits?
notes.back: Extract.
notes.choices:
A) Extract
B) Classify
C) Generate
D) Segmentation
notes.choicesExplained: B chooses from fixed categories. C writes new values freely. D splits content; it is not a field method.
notes.explanation: Extract takes values directly as they appear in document content.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Extract**: Directly extract values as they appear in the input content (supported for documents only)

notes.front: Each support call must be labelled “complaint”, “query” or “praise”. Which field method fits?
notes.back: Classify.
notes.choices:
A) Extract
B) Classify
C) Generate
D) Source grounding
notes.choicesExplained: A only works on documents and copies values verbatim. C writes free text. D locates where a value came from.
notes.explanation: Classify picks a value from a predefined set of categories.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Classify**: Classify content from a predefined set of categories, such as call sentiment or chart type

notes.front: A podcast publisher wants a two-sentence episode summary for each recording. Which field method fits?
notes.back: Generate.
notes.choices:
A) Extract
B) Classify
C) Generate
D) prebuilt-read
notes.choicesExplained: A is for documents and copies existing text. B only picks categories. D is a document text extractor.
notes.explanation: Generate produces values freely, such as summaries of audio conversations.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: **Generate**: Generate values freely from input data, such as summarizing an audio conversation

notes.front: A firm must pull tables and section headings out of annual reports, not just the words. Which prebuilt analyzer fits?
notes.back: prebuilt-layout.
notes.choices:
A) prebuilt-read
B) prebuilt-layout
C) prebuilt-imageSearch
D) prebuilt-callCenter
notes.choicesExplained: A gives text without layout analysis. C describes images. D analyses call recordings.
notes.explanation: prebuilt-layout adds tables, sections and document structure; prebuilt-read gives text without layout analysis.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “prebuilt-layout” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Extracts content and layout elements such as words, figures, paragraphs, and tables from documents. * Identifies document structure, including sections and formatting.

notes.front: A bank wants names and expiry dates from customers’ passports with no setup of its own. What should it use?
notes.back: The prebuilt identity document analyzer (prebuilt-idDocument).
notes.choices:
A) The prebuilt identity document analyzer
B) A custom analyzer built from scratch
C) prebuilt-videoSearch
D) A guardrail
notes.choicesExplained: B needs setup the bank wants to avoid. C analyses videos. D is a safety control, not an extractor.
notes.explanation: Prebuilt analyzers are ready to use for common document types.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Prebuilt analyzers are ready-to-use tools that streamline common content processing tasks.

notes.front: A prebuilt invoice analyzer misses two fields a retailer needs. What is the suggested route?
notes.back: Use the prebuilt analyzer as a template for a custom analyzer and add the fields.
notes.choices:
A) Use the prebuilt analyzer as a template for a custom analyzer
B) Switch to prebuilt-read
C) Raise the confidence threshold
D) Use a vision chat model
notes.choicesExplained: B returns text only, with no fields. C changes routing, not which fields exist. D is not an analyzer.
notes.explanation: Starting from the template keeps its existing schema, which you then extend.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools”, “Customize prebuilt analyzers” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Use any prebuilt analyzer as a template for creating a custom analyzer that better fits your specific needs.

notes.front: An invoice total comes back with a confidence score of 0.41 and weak grounding. What should the workflow do?
notes.back: Send it for human review.
notes.choices:
A) Send it for human review
B) Post it to the ledger automatically
C) Delete the invoice
D) Change the output to Markdown
notes.choicesExplained: B is for high-confidence, grounded results. C loses data. D changes format, not reliability.
notes.explanation: Low-confidence or poorly grounded extractions should be routed to people, not automated.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools document solutions”, “Field extraction” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Use confidence scores and source grounding to route low-confidence or insufficiently grounded extractions for human review.

notes.front: A team is feeding thousands of manuals into a search index for a RAG chat assistant. Which output format suits?
notes.back: Markdown.
notes.choices:
A) Markdown
B) `JSON` for automation only
C) Audio
D) An image
notes.choicesExplained: B suits automation and analytics workflows. C and D are not Content Understanding output formats.
notes.explanation: Markdown output is meant for search and retrieval scenarios.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?”, “Key components of Content Understanding” (MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs on GitHub)
notes.evidence: Content can be output as Markdown for search and retrieval scenarios

notes.front: A contact centre wants summaries, sentiment and the people mentioned in each recorded call, without building an analyzer. What fits?
notes.back: prebuilt-callCenter.
notes.choices:
A) prebuilt-layout
B) prebuilt-callCenter
C) Real-time speech to text only
D) prebuilt-imageSearch
